changelog: Insert a new Core Principle that explicitly asks the scorer to check for immediately following scope-bearing material (negation, quantifiers, rescoping adverbials, contrastive coordinators, disambiguating head noun/verb) and to lower a cut's rank when present — directly addresses the primary finding.

Change C5 to keep the warning about cuts inside long noun groups but allow internal cuts when the left fragment is a clear head and the right only adds modifiers/clarifiers, enabling denser short-latency segmentation as the critique recommends.
Replace example E1 with the measured labeled example en_us_733 (high gap, scope-bearing immediate material) so the model sees a worked case showing the dangerous pattern.

Replace C2 (Cohesion) to allow and prefer internal cuts inside noun groups when the left fragment is a clear identifiable head and the right only adds modifiers, addressing the primary finding that the prompt overgeneralizes 'don't cut inside long noun groups' and needs denser short-latency segmentation.

Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_1116 to show an immediate scope-bearing reversal ('except' after comma) so scorers learn to lower ranks for cuts before such material (addresses the primary finding).

Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_103 to demonstrate a long noun-group where an internal cut can leave a clear head on the left and modifiers on the right, encouraging denser short-latency segmentation.

Insert a new Core Principle after C5 that permits internal noun-group cuts when the left fragment is a clear syntactic head and the right only adds modifiers, to enable denser, cohesive short-latency segmentation (addresses the primary finding).
